newsitem.title: GERMANY: Still no decision on Bonn budget freeze - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Still no decision on Bonn budget freeze - ministry.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has still not decided whether to slap a freeze on extra state spending, but will make up his mind soon, ministry spokeswoman Barbara Eckrich said on Wednesday.
Repeating comments made by Waigel last weekend, Eckrich told reporters "the question is open, he has not yet made up his mind and cannot rule it out in the next few weeks."

A surge in unemployment to nearly 4.7 million in January -- the highest since 1933 -- has piled the pressure on Waigel to limit spending to meet the government's budget deficit target this year and qualify for European monetary union.
The government is standing by its forecast of a deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product -- just below the Maastricht treaty ceiling of three percent.
But many economists believe that Germany will overshoot. A Reuter survey of over 30 economists on Wednesday showed that they on average predicted a deficit this year of 3.05 percent of GDP.
